text:
maria: FYI opened a docs PR for the error-reference: context-limit trimming + fallback heuristics + SDK samples. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4123 Need a quick review before EOD. Main asks: add JS/py snippets showing how to trim prompts, an async retry with exponential backoff handling 429s/timeouts, and a short example of fallback to a cheaper model when tokens cost spikes. Also found a broken link to model-variants that needs fixing.

alex: Taking a look now. Is this meant to replace the existing context-trim section or be an appendix? Want to avoid duplication.

maria: Appendix for now — we want a minimal change so existing pages keep working. The appendix will be a "how-to" checklist and copy-paste snippets.

tj: Heads up: the JS SDK sample currently in the PR uses client.stream(), which we deprecated last quarter. Suggest we show the new pattern (client.responses.stream or client.responses.create with streaming) and a short non-streaming example. I can patch that.

alex: Also call out Retry-After header vs exponential backoff. People assume Retry-After is always set for 429 but not always. A small snippet showing how to parse header and fallback to backoff if missing would be helpful.

rachel: CI just reported a failing example in examples/trim.md — the python snippet imports from redwood_sdk.oldpath.

docs-bot: lint-check failed on examples/trim.md line 42: trailing whitespace.

maria: Thanks — will push quick fixes for the import and trailing whitespace in a sec.

maria: Pushed updates: fixed import path, removed trailing whitespace, added the JS streaming + non-streaming examples, and linked to the model-variants page using updated slug. Commit: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/commit/abc123

tj: Nice. I left one comment: the Python snippet uses param name "timeout_secs" but our SDK is using "timeout" now. I'll open a tiny patch to align. Also updating the JS to prefer responses.create for short synchronous calls. Example I suggest adding:

```js
// short sync call with fallback to cheaper model if tokens > threshold
const res = await client.responses.create({model: "redwood-alpha-3", input: prompt, max_tokens: 150});
if (estimateTokenCost(res) > TOKEN_THRESHOLD) {
  // async fallback path
  await client.responses.create({model: "redwood-beta-quant", input: trimPrompt(prompt), max_tokens: 120});
}
```

alex: Small nit: in the retry snippet please show reading Retry-After header and a capped exponential backoff. Something like:

```py
retry_after = int(resp.headers.get("Retry-After", "0"))
if retry_after > 0:
    sleep(retry_after)
else:
    backoff = min(base * (2 ** attempts), MAX_BACKOFF)
    sleep(backoff)
```

rachel: I added a review comment that the fallback-to-smaller-model section should include a cost/SLO caveat — i.e., fallback reduces cost but may increase hallucination risk; we should encourage evals on real prompt sets.

maria: Good call — added a short "tradeoffs" paragraph and a link to the evals playbook. Also updated the examples/trim.md to reference the snippet files under /examples/code.

alex: Looks good to me. Approving. :shipit:

tj: I'll push the tiny param-name fix in ~2m and then approve.

docs-bot: PR #4123 merged by maria at 1765432256.

maria: Thanks everyone! If anything else pops up, we can follow up in a fresh thread for the diagram/flow doc. :tada:
